subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging (Novacorp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Greene <sophie@novacorp.io>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging (Novacorp)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for taking time to meet today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we’re aligned. If I missed anything, please flag it and I’ll update.

Key pain points you shared
- Need to run customer-facing GenAI features with strong PII controls (names, payment tokens, SSNs).
- Current logs are ingested into S3 and retained long-term; legal wants tighter retention and access controls.
- Auditability: security team needs immutable audit logs and proof of redaction for sampled requests.

Current stack
- Data lake: AWS S3 + Glue
- Analytics: BigQuery (exported subsets)
- Key management: AWS KMS (planned HSM evaluation)

Success criteria for an evaluation
- Ability to disable or opt-out logging for specific endpoints and clients.
- Configurable retention by data class (PII vs metadata).
- In-line redaction for PII before it is persisted.
- Audit logs with exportable attestations for compliance reviews.

Redwood capabilities (high level)
- Per-route logging controls (enable/disable), prefix-based KV cache that can be configured to avoid storing inputs.
- Region-aware storage and customer-managed KMS/HSM support for keys.
- Structured audit logs with immutable append-only store and export hooks (we can provide SOC 2 attestation and sample logs).

Proposed next steps
1) I’ll send our security profile + mutual action plan (attached).
2) Proposed: Tech deep dive with your infra/security (60 min) — options: Tue 9 Mar or Wed 10 Mar.
3) We’ll provision a short evaluation (dedicated trial) scoped to the routes you care about so you can validate redaction/retention behavior.

Attachments: redwood_security_profile.pdf (summary + SOC2), mutual_action_plan.xlsx (MVP evaluation plan)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with calendar options.
\Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198
\---
Note: This is a post-call recap. Internal recipients only: Vivek is on the thread for visibility and to coordinate Dedicated/trial sizing.

From: Sophie Greene <sophie@novacorp.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Data privacy & logging (Novacorp)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from the security and product teams:
- Retention: For PII we need default retention of 30 days, with the ability to extend to 90 days per customer opt-in. For non-PII metadata (latency, status codes) we keep up to 12 months.
- Logging controls: We need per-client toggles and an API to programmatically disable logging for specific API keys/services.
- Redaction: Prefer deterministic redaction on the agent/input side (regex + ML tagger) but we also need server-side verification that redaction occurred before anything is persisted.
- Keys: Our legal team prefers HSM-backed keys for any customer encryption keys; AWS KMS with CloudHSM meets this.

We’re interested in the dedicated trial and a security call. Tue 9 Mar is good for our engineering lead and security; can you do 10:00–11:00 PT? Also: can you provide a sample of the audit export format (JSON lines) so our security team can validate ingestion?

One more ask: For the evaluation we’ll need an option to prevent transcripts from being retained by default (i.e., treat transcript storage as opt-in).

Thanks —
Sophie Greene
Head of Product, Novacorp
Sophie.Greene@novacorp.io

Dev — forwarding the thread. Novacorp wants tight retention windows (30d for PII by default), per-client logging toggles, programmatic controls, and HSM-backed keys. They also want server-side verification that redaction occurred.

Ask: can you draft a short tech note (1–2 paragraphs) we can share with their security team documenting:
- How Redwood supports no-persist routes and per-route logging toggles,
- Options for in-line redaction vs server-side verification,
- Retention enforcement (config store + job that purges S3/DB blobs), and
- How we integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM (required config + limitations).

If possible, include the specific retention config keys and the expected delay between purge job runs (e.g., hourly/daily). We want to get this to them before the Tue 9 Mar call.

Thanks —
Marissa
